title: Deprecation scenarios simulator and compatibility litmus suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a deterministic, replayable test harness and simulator for deprecation scenarios that exercises combinations of streaming, tool/function calling, and structured-output behavior flags. The goal is to reliably detect behavioral regressions introduced by runtime changes or flag flips and provide automated migration guidance for SDKs and clients. This ticket covers the simulation harness, test corpus, a compatibility litmus suite, and integration with CI and the console telemetry pipeline.
background: We have frequent small runtime and kernel changes that can subtly alter streaming boundaries, toolcall ordering, or structured output validity. Existing regression tests are fragmented: unit tests validate kernels, e2e smoke tests run on a handful of prompts, and manual canaries catch many regressions late. We need an automated way to exercise cross-flag combinations (e.g., streaming=true + tool_calls=v2 + structured_output=strict) and compare outputs against baselines with tolerances defined by policy, plus migration hints when differences are detected.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible simulator that can replay recorded client traces against multiple runtime flag matrices and model variants
A litmus test suite of ~250 canonical prompts covering streaming breakpoints, interleaved tool calls, and common structured-output schemas
CI integration: failing litmus tests block runtime PRs unless explicitly approved with a documented mitigation
Automated diff reports that summarize semantic vs. syntactic differences and recommend migration actions (flag toggles, SDK shims, or prompt adjustments)
Console integration: surface compatibility risk scores per release and per-customer (anonymized) with links to failing prompts and example deltas
implementation_steps: Design flag matrix representation and canonical combination generator (owner: Marco)
Extend existing request recorder to capture KV-cache state, per-token timing, and tooling invocation metadata (owner: infra team)
Build replay engine that can run traces deterministically against local runtime builds and hosted preview images
Create litmus prompt corpus: collaborate with PMs and SDK teams to collect edge cases and customer-filing examples
Implement diff engine with heuristics: structural JSON schema comparison, token alignment, and semantic equivalence checks using embedding similarity
Wire CI: add job that runs litmus suite on PRs targeting runtime or API-path changes and publishes structured results
Expose results in Console under 'Compatibility -> Litmus' with per-test debuggable artifacts (request log, transcript, diff)
Draft migration guide templates with actionable remediations for each common failure class
test_plan: Unit tests for replay determinism (seeded randomness, KV-cache resets)
Synthetic regression injection: flip a flag locally and assert the expected subset of litmus tests fail
Golden baseline validation: nightly job to regenerate baselines only via approved change windows
Shadow-run on a subset of hosted traffic (1%): compare live responses to litmus-generated expectations and collect false positive/negative metrics
Post-PR manual review workflow for high-risk diffs: include PM and SDK owners before merging
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (prototype): run simulator against archived traces and produce report artifacts (SRE + Eng review)
Phase 1 (CI integration): add PR gating for runtime-team changes after two successful prototype iterations
Phase 2 (console + customer): surface compatibility risk scores in internal Console and pilot with 3 enterprise accounts
Phase 3 (enforce): require 'compatibility-approved' label for releases with non-zero high-risk litmus failures or automated mitigations in place
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: litmus-suite pass rate per PR and per nightly run
Metric: semantic-delta rate (fraction of tests with embedding-similar outputs below threshold)
Alert: sudden drop in pass rate after a merge -> create incident and auto-open regression ticket with top failing traces
Dashboard: top 10 failing litmus tests linked to recent commits, owners, and suggested mitigations
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: high false positive rate from naive diffs -> Mitigation: use multi-stage comparators (schema -> token alignment -> embedding similarity)
Risk: test corpus doesn't reflect real customers -> Mitigation: seed corpus from opt-in real traces and feedback loop with CS/PMs
Risk: CI becomes slower -> Mitigation: tier tests (fast smoke vs full litmus) and cache deterministic artifacts
Risk: privacy of recorded traces -> Mitigation: PII scrubbers and opt-in policy; retain only anonymized artifacts for Console
